action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's budget posture is still to scale up acquisition: the long-run uptrend is intact, and this kind of phase has historically been when spending to win new and returning users paid back best, especially among active traders. This week calls for applying it carefully: the Binance hack is still being cleaned up, price is about 5% under its 50-day average and the mood is fearful, so add spend in small steps, lead with safety and trust rather than hard offers, and speed up only once price wins back about $81,928. This is a budget-timing guide for the business, not trading advice.

reasons: BTC ($77,538) is about 6% above its 200-day average ($73,152), which is still rising.
Up about 22% over 90 days; about 83% of those days closed above the long-term average.
But price has closed under its 50-day average ($81,928) for 11 days, about 5% below it.
FBI ties the $6 billion-plus Binance theft to North Korea; Fear & Greed sits at 34 (fear).
watch: The long-run trend still points up, but this week rests on Binance reopening withdrawals and finishing its reserve proof. A smooth reopening and a close above $79,000 would steady things, while a close below $76,000 puts the $73,152 average in focus.
analysis: Bottom line: the long-run uptrend still holds, but this week is shaky after the Binance hack. Short term is soft to neutral: Bitcoin has closed under its 50-day average for 11 days, sits about 5% below it and about 10% under its 30-day high, and the mood reads fear (34 out of 100). News is nudging this down a little: the FBI says North Korea stole more than $6 billion from Binance, though Binance says about 90% of affected assets are replaced and it plans to reopen withdrawals on Sunday 1 November (PANews, CNBC). A normal week now swings about $2,978, so a close above $79,000 (top of a typical week's swing) would turn it clearly up, a close below $76,000 (bottom of that swing) would turn it down, and in between it stays choppy. A smooth reopening would steady the mood; until then, lead with trust rather than offers.

The next month is mixed. The 90-day numbers still point up, with price about 22% higher and about 83% of those days closing above the long-term average, but the last 30 days are down about 8%. News is nudging this down too: the Fed held rates at 3.75%-4.00% on 28 October with two officials wanting a rise, and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan says at least two more rises are needed (Reuters via PANews); the next meeting is 8 December. If price wins back $81,928 (the 50-day average) the month firms up, and it only has room to climb above $86,603 (the 90-day high); while it stays under the average, the month keeps fading. Save bigger campaign pushes for that reclaim.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up at a moderate strength. Price is about 6% above its 200-day average and that average is still rising, about 3% over 90 days, though Bitcoin remains 38% below its all-time high. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $73,152 (the 200-day average); if that goes, $67,424 (the 200-week average) is the next floor, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. So far the hack has not broken this picture, and a close below the 200-day average is what would weaken it, which would be the moment to move budget toward keeping existing users.

team_notes.marketing: Stay on the scale-up plan, but in small steps and with trust-led messages while the Binance story plays out. Keep the normal campaign calendar and hold bigger pushes until price is back above about $81,928.

items.why: Binance reports about 90% of affected assets replaced, and the FBI has named North Korea, saying the stolen funds were mostly turned into ETH. DeFi deposits fell 5.3% to about $83.95 billion the day after the hack, the lowest since late August. TRX fell about 7% in a day; reports show the attackers moved 120 million TRX but do not give a clear reason for the fall.
items.marketing_angle: A plain teaching moment on how one incident can spread across many tokens; keep it factual and calm.

sources.title: Binance: About 90% of affected assets backfilled, Proof of Reserves snapshot published

items.why: ICE, the owner of the New York Stock Exchange, deleted its post on a deal with trade.xyz to bring Hyperliquid-style products to the US, then reposted it with softer wording: 'plans to introduce' and 'pending regulatory approval'. Large holders sold more than $100 million of HYPE around the same time, booking profits, and the token is still up about 15% on the week.
items.marketing_angle: Interest in this topic is high, so an explainer on how on-chain trading venues work could draw readers; no token promotion.

items.why: US spot Ether funds have seen 23 straight trading days of withdrawals, the longest run on record, which Glassnode reads as weaker demand from traditional investors. At the same time, the amount of ETH staked hit a record 43.8 million. The two trends point in different directions, and the reports do not tie them together.
items.marketing_angle: A simple 'what is staking' piece fits, as long as yields are explained without promising returns.

items.headline: FBI: North Korea Behind Theft of Over $6 Billion From Binance
items.why: The largest crypto theft on record is now officially tied to North Korea and withdrawals were still shut at last report, which keeps trust shaky, though Binance says about 90% of affected assets are replaced.

items.headline: Fed's Logan: At Least Two More 25-Basis-Point Rate Hikes Needed
items.why: The Fed held rates on 28 October with two officials wanting a rise, and a voting member now says at least two more are needed, so borrowing costs may stay high or climb, which usually weighs on riskier assets.

items.headline: Nasdaq-Listed NXTT Weighs Selling $450 Million of Bitcoin, Citing Binance Hack and Quantum Risk
items.why: A listed company's board cleared the sale or pledging of about 5,833 BTC, citing exchange weakness and quantum risk, a small sign that some corporate holders are rethinking.

items.headline: CFTC Chair on Binance Hack: We Want to Offer Crypto Exchanges a Federal Registration Option
items.why: The US derivatives regulator is pressing a voluntary federal sign-up route for crypto exchanges, which could add protections over time, but it is a stated plan, not a rule.

items.headline: Uber Joins Blockchain Investment Pilot With HSBC, Franklin Templeton and Others
items.why: Uber joining HSBC and Franklin Templeton in a live test of tokenized deposits and funds is another small step of large firms using public blockchains.

summary.short: The Binance hack, now pinned on North Korea by the FBI, still weighs on trust this week, though it is smaller than on Friday because most losses are reported replaced.
summary.medium: A firmer tone from the Fed is the main weight over the coming weeks, with a small company sale plan against a small regulatory plus.
summary.long: Large firms testing tokenized cash and funds is a small positive for the long run.
